meta.description: Expected-goals model (visible angle with a fixed slope plus opponents in the shot triangle, DFL open-play shots)
meta.source: DFL/Sportec open data: Bassek, M., Rein, R., Weber, H., Memmert, D. (2025). An integrated dataset of spatiotemporal and event data in elite soccer. Scientific Data 12:195. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04505-y. Licence: CC-BY 4.0. Aggregate statistics only; no raw, frame-level or person-level data.
meta.licence: CC-BY 4.0 (data); these aggregates are derived statistics with attribution

config.xg_angle_slope_source: Soccermatics angle-only logistic fit, logit(xG) = -3.52 + 2.84 * theta, on 8,451 shots of the 2017/18 Premier League in the open Wyscout data (Pappalardo et al. 2019, Scientific Data 6:236, doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0247-7, CC BY 4.0)

conventions.coordinates: metres, centre origin, team-attacking direction: the team attacks +x, left is +y; pitch 105 x 68 m
conventions.validity: valid samples only (valid_kinematics = true); estimated gap samples never count for speed, peaks or per-90 values
conventions.per90: normalised on measured (valid) time of each player-match (team decision 2026-10-24); see coverage
conventions.ball: ball status and possession are the provider's (never derived from a stationary ball)

notes: Materials/METRICS.md section 9. Open-play shots (DFL ShotAtGoal) located from the trajectories; features measured at the synchronised frame in the shooting team's attacking coordinates: distance_m from the ball to the centre of the goal line; visible_angle_rad = atan2(w x, x^2 + y^2 - (w/2)^2) with w = 7.32 m, x the distance from the goal line and y the lateral offset; opponents_in_triangle = opposing outfield players with valid samples inside the ball-post-post triangle.
Use from Python: insidethegame_data.calibration.xg(distance_m, visible_angle_rad, opponents_in_triangle); features: shot_features(...).
Label: annotated outcome SuccessfulShot (team decision 2026-10-24). Agreement with the tracking goal-line crossing: 13 of 13 annotated goals are also detected as a crossing.
20 of 144 open-play shots could not be located and are left out (0 of them goals).

Model updating (v4.2, Materials/METRICS.md section 9): logit(xG) = a + 2.84 * visible_angle_rad + b * opponents_in_triangle. The angle slope is fixed (Soccermatics angle-only logistic fit, logit(xG) = -3.52 + 2.84 * theta, on 8,451 shots of the 2017/18 Premier League in the open Wyscout data (Pappalardo et al. 2019, Scientific Data 6:236, doi:10.1038/s41597-019-0247-7, CC BY 4.0)); only a and b are fitted on the 124 located open-play shots (13 goals), two parameters as the rule of about 10 events per variable allows (Peduzzi et al. 1996); L2 = 1 on the standardised b. The distance coefficient is 0 (coef[0]): the visible angle already contains the distance. The first fit (three free slopes) gave the angle a wrong, negative sign; it is replaced.
Checks: b < 0 True; 6 m central > penalty spot > edge of the box True; sum of xG 13.00 vs 13 goals; calibration_table; examples.

Leave-one-match-out log loss 0.3398 vs 0.3440 for a constant rate. Use it for relative chance quality (a wider visible angle and fewer defenders give a higher xG); do not read single coefficients as causal effects.

Penalties: a fixed penalty_xg = 0.79 (Opta, as reported by FBref), counted in the team's xG; direct free kicks use the same model; headers and the goalkeeper position have no feature of their own (too few goals).
Opponents with an invalid sample within 20 m of the ball are not counted (never use an invalid value): this happens on 5 shots.

model: logistic regression with the visible-angle slope fixed (model updating, Materials/METRICS.md section 9): only the intercept a and the slope b of opponents_in_triangle are fitted (Newton's method, L2 on the standardised b, intercept not penalised)
